Zhilin set out ten points of difference in full; in outline he said: “According to the ancient Book of Han, it reads, ‘On the twenty-first day of the fifth month of the sixteenth year of Yongping, the day jiyou, Gentleman Ban Gu submitted’;
之遴 is read Zhilin, not Zhi’li. 己酉 is jiyou; the literal also duplicates "the twenty-first day".

Zhilin loved composition and favored archaic forms; with Pei Ziye of Hedong and Liu Xian of Pei he debated texts until they became intimate friends.

Zhilin loved to compose prose and often wrote in ancient style; with Pei Ziye of Hedong and Liu Xian of Pei he constantly discussed books and thereby became close friends.

Later he became chief clerk to the Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Western Gentlemen of the Household, retaining the governorship.

He went out as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Poyang, General Who Campaigns in the West and Governor of Nan Commandery; the Founding Emperor said to him, “Your mother is advanced in years and in virtue alike—therefore I send you home in splendor to fulfill every duty of honor and nurture.”

Once, on Jingzhou staff, he lodged in the Nan Commandery offices and dreamed the former governor Yuan Can said, “You will one day be the broken-armed governor and live here.”
Once, on Jingzhou staff, he lodged in the Nan Commandery offices and dreamed the former governor Yuan Tuan said, “You will one day be the broken-armed governor and live here.”

公羊 is Gongyang, not Gongsun. 鐸椒 is one person, Duo Jiao, not two. 瑕丘 is read Xiaqiu.

After Humu, Dong Zhongshu rose; along the Guliang line, Qianqiu was most firm.
千秋 is the Guliang master Qianqiu, not "Gongsun Qian".
Following in the steps of Humu, Dong Zhongshu flourished; along the line of the Guliang, Gongsun Qian was most steadfast.
Following in the steps of Humu, Dong Zhongshu flourished; along the line of the Guliang, Qianqiu was most steadfast.
千秋 is the Guliang master Qianqiu, not "Gongsun Qian".
His collected works, fifty scrolls in all, circulated abroad.
His collected works, fifty scrolls in all, circulated in the world.
行於世 means circulated in the world, not abroad.

征西 is the prince's general title; it is not a place in Poyang.

Guan Zhong’s seventy-two rulers, counted soberly, yield barely twenty-odd names—Fuxi through Wu, with Gonggong hegemon of the Nine Provinces in between, no emperor’s tally: whence seventy-two Feng-and-Shan kings?

Guan Zhong’s seventy-two rulers, counted for middle antiquity, yield barely twenty-odd lords—Fuxi, Shennong, Nüwa, Dating, Baihuang, Zhongyang, Lilu, Lilian, Hexu, Zunlu, Hundun, Haoying, Youchao, Zhuxiang, Getian, Yinkang, Wuhuai, the Yellow Emperor, Shaohao, Zhuanxu, Gaoxin, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—with Gonggong in between, a hegemon of the Nine Provinces not counted among the emperors: whence seventy-two Feng-and-Shan kings?
The idiomatic version omits the twenty-odd rulers the source lists by name, which are the substance of the argument.

Before the Suiren (the Fire-Driller) through Zhou there was no ruler-and-minister order and hearts were plain—gold paste, jade cases, ascent of the central peak, and carved stone do not belong there.
燧人 is the single legendary sovereign Suiren, counted among the Three Sovereigns, not a plural "Fire-Drillers".
